forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Teignbridge forecasts £0.229m underspend for 2026/27 at Quarter 2, as restructure savings carry into 2027/28
news_drafts.lead:
Teignbridge District Council forecasts a £0.229m underspend on its day-to-day spending for 2026/27, according to the second-quarter monitoring report to the Executive on 3 November. The report says the 2026/27 revenue outturn is forecast to be "a £0.229m underspend against the approved budget". That is a £0.046m adverse movement from the first quarter.

The report sets total revenue expenditure at £20.891m against funding of £20.951m. It says favourable income variances are forecast to more than offset adverse expenditure and funding variances. The forecast surplus is transferred to the General Fund Reserve, pending councillors' consideration as part of the reserves strategy.

A separate paper on budget assumptions for 2027/28 says service restructures "have largely been completed and are contributing to underspends in 2026/27 service budgets". It says the savings from the completed restructures will be incorporated permanently into the 2027/28 budget. The same paper says the corporate vacancy management target of more than £1m, held within Financing Items, will be reviewed and allocated to services.

news_drafts.headline: Teignbridge cuts forecast funding gaps by nearly half as audit work to regain assurance accelerates
news_drafts.lead: Teignbridge District Council faces a disclaimed audit opinion, the lowest form of external audit assurance, for 2025/26 and has held this status since 2020/21. However, the council's financial position is improving. Forecast funding gaps for 2027/28 and 2028/29 have fallen from £3.6 million and £2.8 million to £1.13 million and £0.95 million, driven partly by drawing only £680,000 from reserves in 2025/26 against a budgeted £1.5 million. The Ministry of Housing and Communities and Local Government upgraded Teignbridge's audit assessment ranking from D to C. Regaining assurance work, originally scheduled for 2030–31, is now prioritised to begin in 2027, backed by £42,388 in government grant funding. Internal audits have identified control gaps: licensing income lacks regular reconciliation; the self-build register requires cleansing; and car park audit recommendations from February 2024 remain largely unimplemented, with only two of ten completed. Financial resilience has been marked as a critical audit priority.

findings.headline: The agreed 3.3% pay award adds £0.086m to employee costs, against a 3.0% budget assumption.
findings.detail: Employee costs are forecast £0.204m above budget. Many services are holding vacancies, and the corporate vacancy target of £1.025m offsets these underspends.
findings.matters: A pay award set above the budget assumption is a cost driver that finance directors across the sector will be modelling in their own 2026/27 forecasts.
findings.figures: 3.3% agreed pay award; 3.0% budget assumption; £0.086m cost impact; £0.204m employee cost variance; £1.025m corporate vacancy target
findings.quote: The employee cost variance also includes the impact of the agreed 3.3% pay award (£0.086m), compared with the 3.0% budget assumption

findings.headline: Housing forecasts £1.035m of favourable grant income, mainly from the Crisis and Resilience Fund (CaRF)
findings.detail: The associated grant-funded payments and staffing costs are included in the forecast, so the paper states the income does not represent a £1.035m net saving.
findings.matters: Grant income that is largely matched by grant-funded spending is a distinction a finance director needs to make when comparing headline income figures across councils.
findings.figures: £1.035m favourable grant income; £0.793m of grant income relating to CaRF within the total grant variance; £0.084m lower bed and breakfast costs
findings.quote: The forecast also includes £1.035m of favourable grant income, mainly from Crisis and Resilience Fund (CaRF).

findings.headline: Around £0.200m of budgeted Extended Producer Responsibility expenditure is delayed after the Government deferred film collections from April 2027 to April 2030.
findings.detail: The delay partly offsets the food waste grant loss in the Environmental Services forecast. Members previously approved additional waste establishment posts for 2026/27.
findings.matters: A national deferral of a waste obligation creates a timing saving that other councils should expect to see in their own EPR budgets.
findings.figures: approximately £0.200m delayed expenditure; film collections deferred from April 2027 to April 2030
findings.quote: around £0.200m of budgeted expenditure will be delayed following the Government’s decision to defer the introduction of film collections from April 2027 to April 2030.

findings.headline: Environmental Services loses £0.195m of budgeted food waste grant income, which is no longer expected to be received.
findings.detail: Higher fuel costs of £0.044m add to the pressure. These are partly offset by around £0.200m of delayed Extended Producer Responsibility expenditure following the Government's decision to defer film collections.
findings.matters: Loss of a budgeted food waste grant is a funding change that other councils running weekly food collections may also be exposed to.
findings.figures: £0.195m food waste grant income lost; £0.044m higher fuel costs; approximately £0.200m delayed EPR expenditure; £0.041m adverse variance
findings.quote: the loss of £0.195m of budgeted food waste grant income, which is no longer expected to be received

findings.headline: Officers have identified approximately £2.511m of carry-forward balances for consolidation, from £5.9m held across more than 100 balances at 1 April 2026.
findings.detail: The consolidated balances would be held corporately under the Section 151 Officer and would only be carried forward in future where ring-fenced, externally funded or clearly linked to specific expenditure. Members are asked to recommend the change to Full Council.
findings.matters: Consolidating over 100 individual carry-forward balances into corporate reserves is a governance change other finance directors may face when rationalising their own legacy balances.
findings.figures: £5.9m carry-forward reserves at 1 April 2026; more than 100 individual balances; approximately £2.511m identified for consolidation; £2.111m reallocated carry forwards; £0.400m RCCO
findings.quote: The Council held £5.9m of carry-forward reserves at 1 April 2026 across more than 100 individual balances.
